nodes.label: Geist / Geist Mono Fonts (fontsource)
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted variable fonts via fontsource npm packages; zero CDN request at runtime. One file covers all weights.

nodes.label: D-DIN Font (CDN temporary)
nodes.rationale: D-DIN not in fontsource; using CDN import as temporary measure. TODO: self-host before launch.

nodes.label: Astro 6.4.2 Framework Choice
nodes.rationale: Static output by default; no React/Svelte islands in Milestone 1. Islands added later for charts and scattered-reports stack component.

nodes.label: Plain CSS Custom Properties (no Tailwind)
nodes.rationale: Design tokens in tokens.css. Brief calls for building design system from scratch; hand-crafted token layer serves better than Tailwind utility approach.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages Deploy Configuration
nodes.rationale: Astro's official GH Pages action splits into build + deploy jobs. v3 is current as of Milestone 1.

nodes.label: Render-Blocking Access Gate (dev9 token)
nodes.rationale: Inline script in Layout.astro head; runs before any paint so no flash before redirect. Token dev9 stored in localStorage. Remove block for public launch.

nodes.label: public/CNAME Supersedes Root CNAME
nodes.rationale: Astro copies public/ to dist/, so dist/CNAME is what GitHub Pages reads. Root-level CNAME can be removed.

nodes.label: 3DPR Cover Photo — Rocket on Launchpad at Night
nodes.description: Night-time photo on an outdoor athletic field (artificial turf). A green 3D-printed rocket is mounted vertically on an orange metal launchpad/launch rail frame. A soccer goal is visible in the background. The rocket appears ready for launch. This is the cover/hero image for the 3DPR project.
nodes.norm_label: 3dpr cover photo — rocket on launchpad at night

nodes.label: 3D Printer Running — Early Layer Print
nodes.description: Close-up photo of an FDM 3D printer in operation. The build plate shows early layers of a green filament part being printed — appears to be a small disc or circular component. The printer display reads '56 mm³' (volume printed). Camera lens/nozzle housing visible at top. Material color is olive/yellow-green.

nodes.label: Rocket Body Weight Measurement — 20.2 g
nodes.description: Green 3D-printed rocket body section (tubular body with integrated fins) placed on an Etekcity digital kitchen scale. Scale reads 20.2 grams. Part is FDM-printed in bright green filament. The body tube is hollow/open-ended, with 3 trapezoidal fins integrated at the aft end. Background shows other green parts.

nodes.label: Rocket Fin Assembly — 3D-Printed Green Fins
nodes.description: Close-up of the aft section of the green 3D-printed rocket showing the fin assembly. Three swept/trapezoidal fins are integrated into the body tube. A wooden dowel (beige/tan) is visible protruding from the aft opening — likely a launch rod guide or motor mount. Surface shows FDM layer lines with some post-processing marks. Rocket laid horizontally on a gray surface.

nodes.label: 3DPR Launchpad Setup — Night Launch on Athletic Field
nodes.description: Identical to cover photo — night-time outdoor launch on an artificial turf athletic field. Orange metal launchpad structure with the green 3D-printed rocket mounted on the rail. Soccer goal visible in background. Scene is pre-launch or at moment of launch ignition. Possibly UCLA campus athletic field.
nodes.norm_label: 3dpr launchpad setup — night launch on athletic field

nodes.label: Rocket Nose Cone — 3D-Printed with Parachute Cord
nodes.description: Green 3D-printed rocket nose cone connected to the body tube, shown horizontally on a gray surface. The nose cone is ogive/conical shaped. A braided cord or string (parachute/recovery cord) is tied around the nose cone shoulder/coupler joint — indicative of a recovery system attachment point. Layer lines from FDM printing are visible.
nodes.norm_label: rocket nose cone — 3d-printed with parachute cord

nodes.label: Prototype B — Yellow 3D-Printed Rocket (Disassembled)
nodes.description: Two yellow 3D-printed rocket components on a classroom/school desk: (1) the main body tube with integrated fins standing upright — fins are wide swept deltas — and (2) the nose cone section placed separately beside it. Both are FDM-printed in bright yellow filament. The body has a single fin visible and a small tab/slot feature. Context appears to be a classroom setting (chair backs visible). This is likely an earlier prototype iteration (Prototype B) before the final green version.

nodes.label: 3DPR Team Photo — Launch Night
nodes.description: Group photo of six students (5 visible fully, 1 partially) on an outdoor athletic field at night under stadium lights. They are holding the green 3D-printed rocket together with outstretched hands. All are smiling. Background shows a lit sports field, stands/bleachers, and a building. This is the project team celebrating after the launch. The green rocket is clearly visible being held collaboratively.

nodes.label: 3D-Printed Rocket (3DPR) Project
nodes.author: Manav Patel
nodes.description: Student aerospace project to design, 3D print, and launch a small rocket. Iterated through at least two prototypes (yellow Prototype B, final green version). Components include body tube, fins, nose cone, wooden motor mount dowel, and parachute recovery cord. Launched from an orange metal launchpad on an outdoor athletic field at night, likely UCLA campus.

nodes.label: FDM 3D Printing — Manufacturing Method
nodes.description: Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) 3D printing used to manufacture all rocket components. Visible in print-in-progress photo. Green and yellow filament used across iterations.

nodes.label: Orange Metal Launch Rail Frame
nodes.description: Orange painted steel/metal launchpad structure with launch rail guides. Holds the rocket vertical for launch. Used at the night launch event on the athletic field.

nodes.label: Parachute Recovery System
nodes.description: Recovery system using a parachute attached via braided cord tied to the nose cone shoulder. Visible in nose_cone.jpg.

nodes.label: Rocket Body Mass — 20.2 g
nodes.description: Measured mass of the 3D-printed rocket body (with fins) is 20.2 grams, per Etekcity scale readout.

nodes.label: Nosecone Cap CAD Model (Context View)
nodes.description: CAD model of nosecone cap shown in Autodesk Fusion 360 (file named 'nose cone_gmpr'). The view shows a rectangular/block-shaped cap component seated in a curved nosecone shoulder/coupler region. The tab 'GMPR-draft_copy' is also open. The design shows the cap fitting into a recessed pocket in the nosecone body.

nodes.label: Nosecone Cap CAD Model (Closeup/Detail View)
nodes.description: Close-up CAD view of the nosecone cap block component in Fusion 360 (file 'GMPR-draft_copy'). The component appears as a rectangular/trapezoidal solid block with a beveled or chamfered bottom edge. The geometry suggests this is a structural retaining cap or plug for the nosecone tip. The mesh/grid texture hints at a lightweight or patterned internal structure.

nodes.label: Nosecone Cap 3D-Printed Prototype
nodes.description: Physical 3D-printed prototype of the nosecone cap, shown in hand. The part is orange/amber colored FDM-printed plastic, cylindrical cup-shaped with a flat top and stepped/flanged base. Visible layer lines indicate FDM 3D printing. The design includes a small notch/slot feature on the side wall. The prototype appears to be a fit-check or form validation piece for the nosecone assembly.

nodes.label: GMPR Nosecone Assembly
nodes.description: Conceptual node representing the full GMPR composite rocket nosecone assembly, of which the cap is a sub-component.

nodes.label: GMPR Composite Rocket Project
